raw_title: Through Different Lenses: Comparing AI-Generated Imagery and Press Photography in Visual War Representation
raw_abstract: As AI-generated images become increasingly available and prominent in media production and consumption, they present new opportunities but also raise ethical and practical concerns in newsrooms. This study examines how synthographs—photorealistic images created by generative AI models—offer distinct visual war representation compared to professional photojournalism. Using a mixed-method approach, we analyzed 1028 visuals: 212 photographs from the World Press Photo Award (WPA) 2020–2024 and 816 synthographs generated by Midjourney AI using the same captions as the WPA photos. Our findings show that, on a superficial level, synthographs shared similar thematic elements and motifs with human-made photos. However, upon a closer examination, significant differences emerged in the subtleties of visual framing. Journalistic photographs showed deliberate framing choices focusing on the violence and destruction of war and diverse vision aesthetics to emphasize emotion, suffering, and resilience. Synthographs relied on a more standardized composition of pictures and stereotypical visual symbols. This research highlights limitations and biases inherent in AI-generated war imagery, reinforcing the importance of preserving ethical and nuanced storytelling in professional photojournalism.

plain_summary_en: This paper studies Through Different Lenses: Comparing AI-Generated Imagery and Press Photography in Visual War Representation. In plain terms, it asks what is happening, why it matters for public communication, and what evidence the authors use. The likely focus is Representation (politics), Photography, Photojournalism, Computational photography. The abstract suggests a mixed methods approach, which makes the work useful for understanding how communication changes in everyday life.
